label: Candidate: Senior Cloud Architect
jd: Senior Cloud Architect: design resilient distributed systems on AWS, manage multi-region data replication, optimize p99 latency, and mentor engineering teams on chaos engineering and system design. 5+ years of experience.
resume:

transcript:
Interviewer: Welcome, Vikram. Tell me about your multi-region active-active architecture.
Candidate: We ran dual active regions for high availability. We chose DynamoDB Global Tables with custom partition keys to prevent hot partitions across shards. For cross-region sync, we maintained vector clocks to detect concurrent writes and applied deterministic last-write-wins resolution with nanosecond timestamps. Our measured p99 replication latency stayed under 95 milliseconds even during peak traffic.
Interviewer: How did you handle network partitions between regions?
Candidate: We tuned the read consistency levels. Non-critical reads used eventual consistency from the local region, while financial ledger operations used local quorum reads with conditional expressions to prevent double spends during transient network splits.
Interviewer: Your resume mentions chaos engineering GameDays. How did you structure those?
Candidate: We used Chaos Mesh in our staging clusters. I injected 30 percent packet loss and induced sudden region failover during simulated peak load. In our first drill, we caught a cascading retry storm in our payment gateway. I fixed it by introducing jittered exponential backoff and circuit breakers with Resilience4j.
Interviewer: Tell me about your mentorship of the four engineers.
Candidate: I ran weekly 1-on-1 architecture pairing sessions where we walked through distributed consensus algorithms like Raft and Paxos. I stepped back and let each mentee lead an RFC and present it to our architecture review board. All four successfully owned major production microservices.
